basic_info: 45-year-old male presenting with pain, redness, and warmth in the big toe for approximately two weeks, affecting mobility.
present_illness: Onset two weeks ago, pain exacerbated by walking or movement, associated with redness and warmth. No prior treatment mentioned. No swelling or drainage noted. Symptoms have been worsening over the past couple of weeks. No history of similar episodes. The patient mentioned that the pain worsened last week during a trade show, and it has been red and warm to the touch. No recent blood tests or imaging studies performed. No systemic symptoms reported. No fever, chills, or fatigue reported.
past_history: No history of gout, arthritis, diabetes, or similar conditions. No prior illnesses, operations, trauma, allergies, or personal history reported. Family history: None of the close relatives have had gout, arthritis, or similar conditions.
physical_exam: Physical examination: The big toe is red, warm, and tender to touch. There is mild swelling, and a bump or spur is visible on the top of the joint. The skin around the area appears irritated. No drainage is noted. Mobility is affected due to pain.
aux_exam: Auxiliary examination: X-ray of the big toe joint showed a large spur on the top of the joint, significant cartilage loss, and evidence of arthritis, consistent with hallux rigidus. The patient denies a history of gout, hyperuricemia, or related conditions and has not had any blood tests for uric acid levels. No recent trauma or injury to the affected toe was reported.
